name: Frank Moran
life: “I still remember pouring tea for somebody who had searched our flat.” On Friday, near the downtown fountain, Frank keeps a little time free to hear who is playing at the far end of the park.
voice: I was handing out biscuits and learned that offering a uniformed stranger food takes nerve on both sides.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a dark green knitted vest and a watch on a cracked leather band. Frank has heavy brows and an unusually delicate jaw, with short, uneven waves that refuse to lie flat. Frank touches a knuckle to the chin when searching for a word during a conversation.
personality: Likes beautiful, unnecessary things and gets cross with people who mistake poverty for a lack of taste. Frank takes longer choosing a cheap birthday card than an expensive coat.
agenda: To offer both sides refreshments on the same terms.
family: Ansel Perry is Frank’s older cousin. Frank remembers the birthdays. Ansel asks what the birthday guest would like this year. A present that was perfect at sixteen may be completely wrong at forty. They take the trouble of finding out. Asked about *The first straight paycheck*, Ansel says, “My shop window went through in one of our old rows.”
connections: Gloria Sloan. A warm drink at the gathering becomes a reason to ask before publishing the photograph.

reactions.situation: An officer asks whether the wet event should still count as a hearing
reactions.response: Frank asks who missed the chance to speak before calling the hearing complete.

reactions.situation: A street musician can't finish a familiar song
reactions.response: Frank keeps listening through the pause and lets the musician choose the next note.
